name: OPA356AIDBVR
title: OPA356, OPA2356: 200 MHz CMOS voltage-feedback op amps with rail-to-rail output
summary: OPA356 (single) and OPA2356 (dual) are fast CMOS voltage-feedback amplifiers for video and other wideband work: 450 MHz at unity gain, 200 MHz gain-bandwidth and 360 V/µs slew rate, while staying stable at a gain of +1. They run from one 2.5 V to 5.5 V supply (or ±1.25 V to ±2.75 V), take inputs from 100 mV below the negative rail to 1.5 V under the positive one, and swing the output to within 100 mV of either rail. Each channel draws 8.3 mA, can drive a back-terminated 75 Ω cable, and is guarded by a thermal shutdown.

circuits.title: Gain of +2 driving a capacitive load through a series resistor
circuits.description: A non-inverting stage with a gain of 2 set by two 604 Ω resistors, RF from the output to -In and RG from -In to ground. RS sits between the amplifier output and the load capacitance CL, outside the feedback loop. The best RS falls as CL grows, from about 100 Ω near 2 pF to about 24 Ω at 100 pF; the response curves use 80 Ω with 5.6 pF, 36 Ω with 47 pF and 24 Ω with 100 pF. A 1 kΩ resistor from VO to ground may be added as a load.

parts.note: chosen with CL: 80 Ω for 5.6 pF, 36 Ω for 47 pF, 24 Ω for 100 pF

notes: Typical conditions: VS = 5 V, VO = 0.1 Vp-p, ground at VS/2.

circuits.description: The amplifier with +In grounded and a gain of +2 from two 604 Ω resistors, RF from the output to -In and RG from -In to ground. ZO is the impedance looking back into the output node.

operation.text: OPA356 holds one amplifier (SOT23-5 or SO-8) and OPA2356 two (MSOP-8 or SO-8). They are CMOS voltage-feedback amplifiers with 450 MHz unity-gain bandwidth, 200 MHz GBW, 360 V/µs slew rate, 3 pA input bias current and 8.3 mA per channel; the input range includes ground and the output is rail-to-rail to within 100 mV. The two channels of the dual are built separately, so they do not interact and crosstalk is low; it is -90 dB at 5 MHz. All versions are specified from -40°C to +125°C.
A voltage-feedback CMOS design with 200 MHz gain-bandwidth and 360 V/µs slew rate that remains stable down to a gain of +1 V/V, so it works as a voltage follower.
Inputs work from 0.1 V below V- up to 1.5 V below V+. Ground is inside that range, which suits single-supply use on supplies up to 5.5 V.

Performance is specified over 2.7 V to 5.5 V (±1.35 V to ±2.75 V) and the part operates over 2.5 V to 5.5 V (±1.25 V to ±2.75 V). 7.5 V across the supplies is the absolute maximum; beyond it the part can be permanently damaged.

High-frequency layout practice applies: large ground planes, short direct signal traces and a bypass capacitor at the V+ pin. Copper area also sinks heat from the amplifier. Sockets are not recommended for high-speed amplifiers.

Minimum recommended bypass: 10 µF ceramic. A parallel tantalum of 1 µF or more helps when the load resistance is low. Very low harmonic and intermodulation distortion requires adequate bypass capacitance.
The output can drive a standard back-terminated 75 Ω video cable. With back-termination the cable appears to the amplifier as a 150 Ω resistive load rather than a capacitive one.

Typical short-circuit current exceeds 200 mA, and an on-chip thermal shutdown guards against excessive junction temperature: it disables the amplifier at 160°C and re-enables it below 140°C. Continuous DC output current above ±60 mA is not recommended; the output voltage swing against output current curves give the limits.
Internal ESD diodes connect every pin to both supplies. They also provide overdrive protection when the source or a series resistor limits the pin current to 10 mA.

Capacitance on the output raises peaking: at G = +2 with no series resistor, 47 pF and 100 pF give several dB of peak near 100 MHz. A resistor RS between the output and the load, sized to the load capacitance, flattens the response; see the recommended RS curve.
OPA356-Q1 is an automotive version qualified to AEC-Q100; OPA2356-EP is an enhanced-product version for defence, aerospace and medical use.
